title: Artificial Intelligence in Financial Customer Relationship Management: A Systematic Review of AI-Driven Strategies in Banking and FinTech
authors: Mosa Sumaiya Khatun Munira, Shaharima Juthi, Aklima Begum
venue: American Journal of Advanced Technology and Engineering Solutions, 1(1), 20-40
tldr: Systematically reviews 83 studies on AI in financial CRM, finding AI-powered tools reduced response times by 57%, operational costs by 38%, and improved fraud detection efficiency by 74%.
problem_and_motivation: Financial institutions face challenges in managing vast datasets, adapting to dynamic customer behaviors, and maintaining competitive advantage. Traditional CRM systems rely on rule-based automation and structured data analysis, limiting their ability to personalize interactions and detect fraud effectively. The financial services industry needs systematic evidence on how AI-driven CRM strategies impact customer engagement, operational efficiency, fraud detection, and regulatory compliance.
approach: Conducted a systematic review of 83 scholarly studies including peer-reviewed journal articles, industry reports, and financial institution case studies.
Focused on five key AI application areas in financial CRM: customer engagement, fraud detection, predictive analytics, regulatory compliance, and marketing strategies.
Used thematic analysis to categorize AI applications and synthesize quantitative outcomes across case studies.
Compared AI-driven CRM performance metrics against traditional approaches using quantitative impact data from multiple institutions.
Analyzed AI technologies including chatbots, NLP sentiment analysis, machine learning for credit scoring, and anomaly detection for AML.
Examined ethical considerations including algorithmic bias, data privacy, and transparency in AI-driven financial decisions.
findings: num: AI-powered chatbots and virtual assistants reduced customer response times by 57% and operational costs by 38%, while increasing retention rates by 28%.
num: AI-driven fraud detection systems reduced false positives by 52%, improved fraud detection efficiency by 74%, and decreased fraud-related losses by 43%.
num: Predictive analytics improved loan approval accuracy by 67%, expedited processing by 29%, and reduced default rates by 23%.
num: AI-driven KYC/AML compliance automation increased compliance accuracy by 58% and reduced regulatory penalties by 37%.
num: AI-powered marketing strategies increased customer engagement by 53% and boosted product adoption rates by 31%.
num: Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) models contributed to a 27% increase in long-term retention and 22% improvement in per-customer profitability.
num: NLP-driven sentiment analysis enabled proactive complaint resolution, reducing churn rates by approximately 30%.
num: Behavioral analytics in fraud detection reduced unauthorized transactions by 80% in real-time monitoring systems.
num: AI-based credit scoring incorporating alternative data improved loan repayment prediction rates by 55% over traditional methods.
num: AI transparency measures reduced algorithmic bias complaints by 35% and improved customer trust scores by 40%.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Provides comprehensive quantified evidence of AI's impact across five CRM dimensions in financial services, aggregating results from 83 studies with specific performance metrics for each application area.
directly_justifies: Quantified benefits of AI-driven chatbots and predictive analytics for customer engagement in financial systems.
Evidence for AI-based fraud detection and credit scoring model performance improvements.
Support for integrating AI-driven KYC/AML compliance automation in financial systems.
limits: Relies on secondary data from published studies and case reports rather than primary experimental data.
Metrics aggregated across heterogeneous institutional contexts may not be universally applicable.
Limited discussion of implementation challenges, costs, and organizational barriers to AI adoption.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Primary topics are AI (4.A), ML algorithms (4.B), fraud detection/AML (5.C), fintech (7.B), customer analytics/CRM (7.E), and system design (11.A).

limitations: Systematic review relies on secondary published data; metrics are aggregate estimates across heterogeneous studies.
Potential publication bias toward positive AI outcomes in the reviewed literature.
Limited longitudinal analysis of AI system performance degradation or maintenance requirements.
Does not thoroughly address data privacy risks and ethical challenges of AI in financial CRM.
Financial impact metrics vary across institutional contexts and may not generalize to smaller institutions.
